title: Does this Goku-inspired redesign look original enough for a mod, or is it still too similar?
author: Anime118247
selftext:
https://i.redd.it/gf6qt8yyft1i1.png

I'm developing an anime-inspired overhaul mod for Elin called **Galaxion**, featuring 100 protagonists, each from a different anime. The example shown here is my attempt at redesigning Goku from Dragon Ball.

I plan to accept financial support to help cover development costs, mainly to keep my subscriptions running. **The finished mod itself will be completely free.**

For anyone unfamiliar with Elin, characters appear as small pixel-art sprites while walking around the game world as you can see in the image where it says elin-style sprite, but when you interact with them, a larger character portrait appears like in the second image. That's why both designs are important when considering copyright.

I have very little knowledge of copyright law. I've seen anime characters that are practically identical to popular anime protagonists with only their names changed and maybe a different hairstyle, while others use designs that are clearly inspired by existing characters but have enough differences to appear original.

I'm trying to understand where the legal boundaries actually are.

The attached design is obviously AI-generated and supposedly different enough from Goku to avoid copyright issues, although even I'm sceptical about that because you can clearly tell its goku but it says its fine.

Before I spend ages designing the other 99 protagonists, I'd like some opinions.

**My main questions are:**

* Is this redesign actually different enough, or is it still too recognisable as Goku?
* How much can you realistically change a character while keeping the original inspiration obvious?
* Does releasing the finished mod for free make any difference legally?
* Could I use temporary original characters while showcasing development, then replace them with the actual anime protagonists when the free mod releases?
* If supporters knew those temporary characters would eventually be replaced with copyrighted characters, could I still face legal consequences even though they're only funding development rather than buying the mod?

For example, imagine I introduced a completely original NPC during development and told supporters, *"This character will guide you through the tutorial, but he'll be replaced by Goku when the mod officially releases."*

Would that still create copyright problems?

I'm not looking to profit from anyone else's characters. I just want to create an anime crossover experience while avoiding legal trouble, especially when people are financially supporting the project.

I'd appreciate advice from anyone familiar with copyright law, particularly regarding fan games and mods. 

  
Oh and i don't know if this changes anything but they would be supporting it through patreon

https://i.redd.it/vkc3g836ht1i1.png
